# Cycle 0044: carried defects

Part 2 of [Issue #83](https://github.com/laststance/codebook/issues/83) and of [the cycle record](0044-wiki-update-and-carried-defects.md), copied in whole from the intake of 2026-10-03 (every finding read against `main` `c549da6`). Under the [cycle rule](../../AGENTS.md#cycle-rule-every-carried-defect-is-fixed-in-the-next-cycle) every row is a task; the cycle closes only when the **Closed** column of every row names the fix and its test (or the recorded evidence that closes it). Rows classified CLOSED or NOT-A-DEFECT at intake are re-checked, not skipped; a row whose evidence does not hold becomes OPEN. UNKNOWN rows start with the inspection their row names.

Totals at intake: 440 rows; OPEN 262, UNKNOWN 35, CLOSED 109, NOT-A-DEFECT 34.

## Group 1: Cycle 0043 (R1 to R19, O1 to O8, N-1 to N-13)

COUNTS: open=39 closed=1 not-a-defect=0

Source read on `main` at `c549da6` (the only commit after merge `e32add3` changes docs only, so the source is the 0.2.27.0 release tree). Paths are relative to `extension/src/` unless they start with `extension/`. Duplicate groups share one fix: **[A]** R1 = O2 = ER11; **[B]** R8 = O1 = R18; **[C]** R10 = O8; **[D]** R7 + O4 (same wording); **[E]** R11 + O5 (same helpers/schema); **[F]** N-9 + N-10 + N-11 (one obstacle, three texts); **[G]** N-5 + N-13(b) (unregistered snapshot resource templates, likely). R4 was reported twice (delivery and red team); one row.

Fixed after that run (`0470aea`): Cause (VS Code 1.140 `workbench.desktop.main.js`, `registerLayoutListeners`): the workbench calls `toggleMaximizedPanel()` whenever the main editor part's visible editors change or a group is activated while the editor area is hidden. A Saved studies choice showed the chosen study's captured source (`showSavedStudy` → `renderSelection` → `showTextDocument`), also 250 ms later through the reader's refresh timer, so every choice ended the maximized state; the panel view kept its scroll offset and the section fell below the fold of the small panel. Fix (`studyWorkspace.ts`): `showSavedStudy` asks `editorAreaHidden()` (new `utils/isCollapsedEditorLayout.ts`: every stacked group of `vscode.getEditorLayout` at the minimum group height, `EDITOR_GROUP_MINIMUM_HEIGHT_PX` = 70). While hidden it selects and publishes the study to the panel only, keeps `studyAwaitingEditorArea`, and the refresh timer leaves the panes alone; `showStudyAwaitingEditorArea` (run by every refresh after its lock) arranges and renders once the area is back, and any explicit entry, selection or placement renders at once. Test: studyWorkspaceLayout "choosing another saved study while the bottom panel is maximized leaves the panel maximized and shows the chosen study in it" (harness: new `maximizePanel` model). Redness: with the deferral reverted (`if (false)`), `harness.isPanelMaximized()` was `false`, expected `true`. Also 7 unit tests of the predicate in `editorLayout.test.ts`. | 0039-N8-b / 0040-N9-img  | In VS Code after the panel was maximized and an entry chosen, the Application group stays collapsed to a strip (layout restore)                                                                                         | OPEN                                                                                              | extension/src/studyWorkspace.ts:9642-9643 (re-arrangement on choice)                                                                               | Native check: maximize panel, choose entry, Application group restored                                                   | **FIXED, NATIVE RE-RUN PENDING**: Native run of 2026-10-04 (VS Code 1.140.0 for Linux, candidate 3 (`b27fa6d6…`, source `258508b`), driver over the public MCP protocol, no chat; private evidence in `codebook-qa/n13p2/`): FAIL. FAIL: the Application group ends as a strip. After choice 2 above (panel maximized, entry a0e4f057 chosen at 02:12:5x) the product itself returned the panel to normal height, and the editor area then showed the group 'login-form.tsx \| codebook · Recorded application \| actions.ts' as a strip of about 35 px under its tab row (no application image visible), with the captured-source group ('Captured-login-form.tsx', line 23 highlighted) taking the rest of the height, and 'codebook · Study' beside them (c08-chosen2.png 6 s after the choice, c09-chosen2-12s.png and c09-crop.png 12 s after: unchanged). codebook_status then: presentation.state 'open', layoutConfirmed false, panes app 1 / source 2 / context 3. After choice 1 (first choice after a live run) the Application group had its normal height (about 385 px, c05-chosen-7s.png). So the strip appears when an entry is chosen with the panel maximized while the Study layout is already up. Second occurrence (02:44): with the panel maximized a seek through the public playback tool returned the panel to normal height and left the Application group as a strip showing only its tab row and the header 'codebook · recorded application · Recorded · 140.00 s' (no image), the summary reading 'The Study arrangement is not confirmed. Focus the existing Study or Application pane, then restore its layout. Opening Repository Wiki does not repair Study.' (u18-max-seek.png); a Play of 39 s ran in that state (u19, u21). Study view and pane controls → Restore then repaired it: Application group at normal height, layoutConfirmed true (u25-restored.png). A plain drag of the panel's border up and back did not leave a strip (u27-details-big.png, u28-crop.png). Limits: VS Code only; two occurrences (a Saved studies choice and a playback seek, each with the panel maximized). The frozen step 'restore the panel' was not performed by the driver: the product itself un-maximized the panel (row 0038-N7-e), and the strip was there when it had. The strip is repaired by the product's Restore control, not by itself. Fixed after that run (`7794af0`): Cause (same bundle, `doRestoreGroup`): opening or revealing an editor in a group whose size equals its minimum runs `arrangeGroups(EXPAND)`; a hidden editor area is laid out with height 0, so every stacked group sits at 70 px and the reveal (`showTextDocument` with `preserveFocus` uses `EditorActivation.RESTORE`) expands the source group: Application at 70 px (its tab row and 35 px), Study pane at its minimum width 220 px, exactly `c08-chosen2.png`. The changed sizes then failed the receipt comparison in `readPresentationState` (`layoutConfirmed` false); that comparison also failed for any status read made while the area was hidden. Fix: (1) the choice no longer reveals into the hidden area (row above); (2) `renderSelection` measures before its `showTextDocument` (`confirmedLayoutBehindHiddenArea`) and, when a confirmed Study layout was revealed into a hidden area (a recorded seek, a Recording press, an agent's selection), applies the confirmed grid again (`reapplyConfirmedLayout`, the same `vscode.setEditorLayout(receipt)` Restore uses after Enlarge); (3) `readPresentationState` returns the retained state for a collapsed measurement instead of unconfirming. Tests: studyWorkspaceLayout "after a saved study was chosen with the bottom panel maximized, restoring the panel shows that study with the Application group at its normal height and the layout confirmed" and "a recorded seek made while the bottom panel is maximized leaves the Application group at its normal height and the layout confirmed". Redness: repair reverted → seek test: Application height `70`, expected `420`; guard reverted → first test: `layoutConfirmed` while maximized `false`, expected `true`; deferral and repair both reverted → first test fails the same way. A native re-run on the new candidate is recorded below when it is done.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

| 0035-O01                                                    | Pressing Recording on the attached live run's own in-progress recording recovers in about 2.1 s (0.1 s over the 2.0 s bound); its load phase took 0.87 s vs 0.33 s for a saved study while the range grew.                                                                     | UNKNOWN-time a Recording press on an in-progress recording with a live run attached; no later cycle measured or changed it | extension/src/studyWorkspace.ts:5076 (loadPlayback)                                                               | Native take: Recording on an in-progress recording recovers within 2.0 s                                           | **FIXED, NATIVE RE-RUN PENDING**: Native run of 2026-10-04 (VS Code 1.140.0 for Linux, candidate 3 (`b27fa6d6…`, source `258508b`), driver over the public MCP protocol, no chat; private evidence in `codebook-qa/n13p2/`): FAIL. Three takes in two live runs paused at their first server stop (actions.ts 32:11), each on the run's own in-progress recording shown at its recorded stop with the session 'Codebook · Recorded learning' stopped from the debug toolbar while the live session stayed paused; one press of Recording in the Learning summary; 30 fps video, per-frame strips. Take 1 (run 9d8adf4e, press 01:57:43, recording 33.99 s long at opening and 132.76 s at the press): first visible response ('Presented 33.06 s / 33.99 s' becomes 'No position presented') at 0.933 s of the strip, new range shown ('No position presented / 132.76 s', 'Loading the selected observation…') at 2.47–2.53 s, recovered ('Presented 33.06 s / 132.76 s — last verified time; end unknown', 'Recorded observation · 33.06 s') at 3.867 s: 2.93 s after the first response (pointer arrived 0.33 s before it, so at most 3.27 s after the press). Take 2 (run 17419b70, X click issued 02:05:07.79, 93.74 s long): first response 0.967–1.033 s, new range 2.20–2.27 s, recovered 'Presented 37.65 s / 93.74 s' at 3.467 s: 2.43–2.50 s. Take 3 (same run, X click 02:05:42.78, 128.78 s long): first response 0.933–1.067 s, new range 2.53–2.60 s, recovered 'Presented 37.65 s / 128.78 s' at 3.800 s: 2.73–2.87 s. All three are over the 2.0 s bound (by 0.4 to 0.9 s, take 1 up to 1.3 s). The time until the new range is shown grows with the recording's length (about 1.2 s at 94 s, 1.5–1.6 s at 129–133 s); the rest (range shown to position presented) was 1.2–1.3 s each time. No failure message in any take; the Call Stack listed the recorded session again and the live session stayed paused (a42-recovered.png, a55-t2-recovered.png, a55-t3-recovered.png); both runs then continued to 'demonstrated'. Limits: The press itself is not visible in a frame; times are counted from the first visible response (takes 2 and 3 were X clicks with no pointer travel; in take 1 the pointer arrived 0.33 s earlier). Frame step 33–67 ms. Host: Linux VS Code through WSLg on Windows with a desktop recorder (gdigrab, 2668 × 2040 px, encoding on the same machine) running and Developer Tools open with a 40 ms focus poll, not the Mac of the 2.1 s observation; no saved-study control take was timed on this host, so the host's own share is not separated. The recording was first opened by the driver (codebook_playback open), because during a live pause the window showed no Study pane and no Recording tab until a recording was open ('Codebook: Focus Explanation' and 'Open Study Workspace' changed nothing visible, a19, a20). The recordings were long (94–133 s) because the run stayed paused while the steps were driven. Fixed after that run (`bde5347`): Two waits found. Load phase: `RecordingStore.read` read and hashed again every frame of the journal, although this session's own writer had just hashed and written them. Measured with `dist` on a synthetic in-progress recording of 35 kB frames: 635–693 ms at 1,065 frames and 1,027–1,035 ms at 1,700 frames (the native recordings held 1,065 unique frames at 94 s and 1,669–1,737 at 130 s; 0.6 ms a frame is the slope of the native takes). Presentation phase: `ReplayDebugger.present` waited the whole `REPLAY_DEBUG_INSPECTION_GRACE_MS` (1.0 s) on every reload, although the paused live session keeps the Run and Debug focus: VS Code focuses a newly stopped session only when no frame is focused or the focused frame is its own (bundle, `handleStop`), so the recorded stop's values are never requested during that wait. Fix: `RecordingWriter.writtenFrame` and `RecordingStore.ownWriter`: an unsealed recording of this session is read without reading its frames back (a recording of another session or a sealed one is still fully read); `ReplayDebugger.foreignPauseFocused` (`vscode.debug.activeStackItem` of another session) commits the stop as `uninspected` at once (the same outcome the takes ended with). Budget before: load 1.2 s at 94 s and 1.5–1.6 s at 130 s (read 0.65 / 1.03 s + about 0.55 s for the debugger replacement, context, archive and preference reads, the reader's `open` and the viewport), presentation 1.2–1.3 s (grace 1.0 s + 0.2–0.3 s for the session start, source, paint receipt and context message): 2.43–2.93 s. Budget after: read 77–78 ms at 1,065 frames and 116–120 ms at 1,700 (measured), load about 0.6–0.7 s; presentation 0.2–0.3 s: about 0.8–1.0 s against the 2.0 s bound (computed, not timed natively). No fixed sleep and no second renderer handshake were found on this path (f052184 had removed the handshake); the reader's `open` inside the load was left as it is. Tests: recordingStore "an in-progress recording of this session opens without reading back the frames its own writer wrote" (redness: `readFrame` calls `1`, expected `0`) with the control "a recording an earlier session left unfinished still has every frame read and hashed when it opens"; replayDebugger "a recorded stop is shown at once, without its values, while a paused frame of another debug session keeps the Run and Debug focus" (redness: `'pending'`, expected `'uninspected'`). A native re-run on the new candidate is recorded below when it is done. |

Cold open 1 (01:33, run 4f46d9c6): dead pane focused 01:33:00.412 (IFRAME.webview, the application group); the reader was opened by codebook_presentation at 01:33:04.9; 01:33:05.299 BODY, 01:33:06.175 a text editor (native-edit-context inside an editor group), 01:33:07.639 the text editor of the upper group, and it stayed there for 89 s through the run that started at 01:33:25 (a10.focuslog.txt). Cold open 2 (02:03, run 17419b70): dead pane focused 02:03:13.772; reader opened at 02:03:19.9; 02:03:20.217 BODY, 02:03:20.802 a text editor, 02:03:22.242 BODY for 0.18 s, 02:03:22.426 and 02:03:23.512 a text editor, stable for 11 s: after the cold open itself the focus is in an editor, not on body. BUT 0.7 s after the run's start (start accepted 02:03:33.76) activeElement became BODY at 02:03:34.477 with the window focused and stayed BODY for 31.7 s, until the first stop revealed its captured source (02:04:06.142, a text editor); 5.5 s later, after the capture was committed, it was BODY again (02:04:11.676) until the next driver action 11 s later. The same pattern is in every live run of this session (run 92c27590: BODY from 01:42:58.799 to 01:44:05.656 and after each committed capture; runs c3a33e7a, 9d8adf4e). So during a live run that follows a cold open, keyboard focus is nowhere (body) for most of the time, with no click made (a57.focuslog.txt). Third variant (02:46:52, run d329eac3): dead pane clicked, then the run was started with no presentation call and opened the reader itself (e01-ready.png: 'codebook · actual page stream · live' above the source): its focus log could not be read (see limits). Limits: FAIL by the row's own criterion (activeElement is body), observed at the live entry and after each capture, not at the close of the dead pane: after the cold open itself an editor had focus in both takes. Whether the body state comes from Codebook closing or replacing the focused captured-source editor or from the editor's own handling of a starting debug session was not separated. The runs were started by the driver over MCP, not from a chat, so 'the chat input keeps focus' was not tested (no chat request was submitted in this session). No key was typed to confirm where input goes while activeElement was body. For the third variant (the run's own start opens the reader from dead panes) the focus log is missing: by then the owner's terminal covered the Developer Tools window and the attempt to read the log through X focus typed into the editor instead (reverted, see log.txt). Fixed after that run (`352287f`): Partly fixed. Cause, from the code path and `a57.focuslog.txt`: every drop to `body` follows a reveal of the leased Application pane with `preserveFocus` true (`BrowserViewport.revealNow`) over the editor that held the focus in the application group; VS Code hides the focused editor pane and, because focus is to be preserved, focuses nothing. It is Codebook's reveal, not the debugger's session start. Three cases: (1) after each committed capture: the debugger opens the paused file in the application group with focus (`debug.focusEditorOnBreak`, focus log 02:04:06.142), and `ConfiguredBrowserRun.capture` reveals the Application pane over it (02:04:11.676 body); (2) 0.7 s after the start of run 17419b70: the first reveal over the learner's own focused tab, which the cold open had left in front (new-d); (3) runs c3a33e7a and 9d8adf4e: the first reveal into the focused empty group. Fixed: case 1. `coversEditorFocusedByPause` (a paused stack item, the pane's group is the active group showing a text editor that is the active text editor, `debug.focusEditorOnBreak` not off) makes the pane take the focus the editor it replaces had. Test: runtime-browserViewport "the Application pane takes the keyboard focus when it is revealed over the file the debugger focused at a pause" (redness: reveal recorded `preserveFocus: true`, expected `false`) with two controls ("… leaves the keyboard focus where it is when it is revealed while no debug session is paused" / "… while the learner turned off debug.focusEditorOnBreak"). Not fixed: cases 2 and 3. The extension API reports the active editor, not which part holds the keyboard focus; a learner typing in the chat has the same `activeTextEditor` and active tab group as one typing in the covered file, so taking the focus there would take it from the chat input on every run started from a chat. Missing: a way to tell editor focus from chat focus (none in the API of VS Code 1.140), or an owner decision that the Application pane may take the focus at a run's first reveal. A native re-run on the new candidate is recorded below when it is done.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
